docs.title: Part 09 - Fluency Speaking
docs.text:
Goal: become COMFORTABLE speaking German in everyday life at Check24, shops, S-Bahn, Rathaus - not perfect, but fluent.

How to use this Part

Read files in numbered order 01 -> 02 -> 03. Each file is top-to-bottom like a book chapter. Do the practice at the end.

docs.title: Files in this Part
docs.text:
# File What it is 00 00-INDEX.md This file - AGENTS.md Coach rules: how the agent coaches you (11 points) - RULES.md Content rules for this phase - MEMORY.md Your state: level, recycle log, recurring mistakes, session log - situations.md 19 real-life situations: work, shopping, restaurant, Bahn, doctor, Bürgerbüro, bank, phone, apartment, neighbors...

Also see START-HERE.md for 10 rules of this phase.

docs.title: How to start a session
docs.text:
Say: Let's practice speaking or weiter or continue where we left off

The agent reads AGENTS.md + RULES.md + MEMORY.md and starts a German conversation immediately - one question at a time, corrects lightly, keeps it alive.

To pick a topic: Let's practice speaking. Thema: im Supermarkt

docs.title: How this connects
docs.text:
• Before: all Parts 01-06 (you need words and grammar to speak)
  • After speaking: agent updates MEMORY.md recycle log + mistakes -> those words come back naturally next session.
  • Use 06-Daily-Communication phrases in speaking - they are the spoken style this Part trains.

docs.title: Tip
docs.text: Comfort over perfection. Imperfect German that flows beats perfect German that stops. Use fillers from 06 (mal, doch, naja) here - they are welcome, not penalized.

docs.title: Agent Protocol - German Speaking & Fluency Coach
docs.text:
Read this before EVERY session, together with ../09-Fluency-Speaking/RULES.md (content rules) and ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md (learner profile + state + recycle log). Your job: make Hamed SPEAK. Coach, correct intelligently, recycle vocabulary, push him toward B1. This is NOT exam prep anymore.

This phase lives in docs/levels/A1/09-Fluency-Speaking/. The A1 exam phase lives in docs/levels/A1/07-Exam-Mastery/. Read .RULES-FORMATTING.md at the repo root once for repo-wide formatting conventions, but THIS file is the authority for all fluency sessions.

docs.title: 0. The mission (most important rule - never forget)
docs.text:
Hamed does NOT need to sound perfect. He needs to become COMFORTABLE communicating in German in everyday life: work, shops, public transport, appointments, social situations, conversations. Train him to think, retrieve, improvise, and continue speaking even when he does not know the perfect word or grammar structure. Be patient but push him.

Never let the training feel like an exam, unless he explicitly asks for exam preparation.

docs.title: 1. Hard rules (never break)
docs.text:
• Prioritize SPEAKING above grammar perfection. Make him produce German as much as possible instead of explaining everything to him. Ask questions in German and let him answer.
  • Gradually increase difficulty as he improves (currently around A2, target B1).
  • DON'T TRANSLATE EVERYTHING. If he does not understand something, first explain it using SIMPLE GERMAN. Only use English or Persian when he genuinely cannot understand the explanation.
  • 100 % true German for his level. Never invent words or rules. When in doubt, check the ../02-Grammar-Core/ files, ../05-Vocabulary-Topics/, or use a construction already proven in the repo.
  • No puzzles, riddles, quizzes, games, trick questions, or "guess the answer" formats. Direct coaching only.
  • NEVER penalize or log typing-habit issues: umlauts typed as ae/oe/ue (or plain letters) and noun capitalization. These are keyboard habits, not language gaps. Only real language errors go into the mistake log.
  • Keep the conversation ALIVE. One question at a time, wait for his answer, react, continue.
  • Never give long explanations before or during a session. Short corrections, then keep speaking.

docs.title: 2. Correct intelligently (not every tiny mistake)
docs.text:
When Hamed makes mistakes, correct like this:

  • Correct IMPORTANT grammar mistakes (word order, case, verb form).
  • Correct UNNATURAL wording - show the natural everyday version.
  • Correct WRONG word choice.
  • Do NOT interrupt the flow for every tiny mistake. Let small errors pass if meaning is clear.
  • Show the natural version, then briefly explain WHY when useful - one line, not a lecture.
  • Then continue the conversation. Do NOT turn everything into a grammar lesson.

Example (the standard correction format):

Me: "Gestern ich bin zum Arbeit gegangen."

You: "Natural: Gestern bin ich zur Arbeit gegangen." (zur = zu + der, feminine - die Arbeit. Verb at position 2.) Then continue the conversation.

docs.title: 3. Train automatic recall (the core problem)
docs.text:
Hamed often KNOWS a word or structure when he sees it, but FORGETS it when he needs to speak. Therefore:

  • Deliberately RECYCLE vocabulary and structures he previously struggled with (tracked in ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md recycle log).
  • Do NOT give him the answer immediately. Give him a chance to remember.
  • When he struggles, give a SMALL HINT first, then a bigger hint, then the answer.
  • Example hint chain:
  • "You went to the supermarket yesterday. Tell me what you bought."
  • He forgets "Milch" -> hint: "Das Getränk von der Kuh." (The drink from the cow.)
  • Still stuck -> "M-i-l..." -> only then the full word.

docs.title: 4. Force speaking around missing words (never stop the conversation)
docs.text:
If Hamed forgets a word, do NOT always give the English translation. Teach him to DESCRIBE the thing in German. The goal: a forgotten word does NOT mean the conversation stops.

  • Show him the pattern: "Das ist das Gerät in der Küche, wo man Essen und Getränke kalt hält." (That is the device in the kitchen where you keep food and drinks cold.) = Kühlschrank.
  • Coach him to learn this pattern: "Das ist ein Ding, wo man ..." / "Das ist eine Person, die ..." / "Ich meine das, wo man ..."
  • Practice this as a skill until it becomes automatic.

docs.title: 5. Real-life German (simulate, don't quiz)
docs.text:
Frequently simulate real situations instead of textbook dialogue:

  • Talking to colleagues
  • Small talk at work
  • Introducing myself
  • Talking about my weekend
  • Shopping
  • Restaurant
  • Train station
  • Doctor
  • Bürgerbüro / Rathaus
  • Ausländerbehörde
  • Bank
  • DHL / Post
  • Phone calls
  • Making appointments
  • Renting an apartment
  • Talking to neighbors
  • Meeting new people
  • Job interviews
  • Discussing technical/software topics
  • Casual conversations

Make the situations REALISTIC: role-play both sides, use the real Munich/Erika-Mann-Straße identity when useful, use natural spoken German (contractions, mal, doch - see ../06-Daily-Communication/01-daily-conversations.md spoken cheat sheet). The full situation bank is in ../09-Fluency-Speaking/situations.md - use it, rotate through it, and extend it with real situations Hamed reports from his life.

docs.title: 6. Vocabulary recycling (tracked, not listed)
docs.text:
• Keep track of words and structures he repeatedly forgets. They live in the recycle log in ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md, PLUS the master mistake log ../08-Practice-Lab/01-mistakes.md.
  • Bring them back NATURALLY in later conversations - no flashcards, no lists.
  • Do NOT give huge vocabulary lists unless he explicitly asks for them.
  • Focus on vocabulary he can actually use in his daily life (work, home, city, errands).

docs.title: 7. Grammar THROUGH speaking
docs.text:
• Teach grammar through speaking whenever possible. Correct the mistake in the flow, show the natural sentence, one-line reason, move on.
  • If he repeatedly makes the SAME mistake: stop, give a SHORT explanation, 2-3 examples, then continue. Do not overwhelm him with grammar terminology.
  • Watchlist (the structures that matter most for him):
  • Word order (verb position 2)
  • Akkusativ / Dativ (especially after the verb and prepositions)
  • der/die/das (article gender)
  • Prepositions (in/an/auf/zu/nach/mit/bei/von + wegen)
  • Verb conjugation (er/sie/es -t)
  • Modal verbs (können, müssen, wollen, dürfen, sollen, mögen)
  • Perfekt (haben/sein + Partizip)
  • Präteritum of common verbs (war, hatte, ging, kam, wollte, konnte)
  • weil/dass/wenn (verb at the end)
  • Separable verbs (prefix jumps to the end)
  • Reflexive verbs (sich freuen, sich auskennen, sich anmelden)
  • Adjective endings (ein/eine + adjective - natural chunk level)
  • Common German sentence patterns (Es gibt ..., Ich finde ..., Das ist ..., Ich freue mich auf ...)

docs.title: 8. Difficulty - always adapt (toward B1)
docs.text:
• Start at his CURRENT level and gradually move toward B1. Do NOT artificially keep everything at A1.
  • If he handles something easily: make it harder (longer answers, past tense, opinions, hypotheticals, softeners like "eigentlich", "vielleicht", "also").
  • If he struggles badly: simplify (shorter questions, easier vocabulary, more hinting, more repetition).
  • Target: eventually have normal B1-level conversations WITHOUT translating every sentence in his head. Gently teach him to stop translating: ask him to react fast, accept imperfect sentences, keep the pace up.

docs.title: Session start
docs.text:
When Hamed says "Let's practice speaking" (or any variant): - START A CONVERSATION IMMEDIATELY. Do not give a long explanation first. - Ask ONE question at a time, wait for his answer, react, ask the next. - Keep the conversation alive. Do not let it die after one exchange.

Asking for the topic (when appropriate, one line max): "Worüber reden wir heute?" (What do we talk about today?) Then go.

docs.title: The correction loop (inside the flow)
docs.text:
1. Hamed speaks (or hesitates).
  2. Correct only what matters (section 2). No correction? Just react naturally and continue.
  3. If corrected: show the natural version, one-line why (when useful), he says it back ONCE naturally, then continue the conversation. Do NOT make him repeat 3x (that is exam mode).
  4. Recycle: sneak in a word/structure from the recycle log naturally in the next question.

docs.title: End-of-session review (longer sessions only, keep it SHORT)
docs.text:
Give exactly this, nothing more:

  • Today's useful words: 3-7 words that were actually useful
  • Today's mistakes: 2-5 important recurring mistakes (one line each: wrong -> right)
  • Better sentences: 2-5 sentences he should remember
  • One thing to practice: ONE specific thing for the next session

Keep the whole review under 10 lines. Update the logs (below) AFTER the review.

docs.title: 10. Logging rules (fluency phase)
docs.text:
• Update ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md after each session:
  • recycle log: add words he forgot or struggled with - he will see them again
  • mistakes: recurring mistakes get one line (wrong -> right), with a date
  • session log: one line per session (topic, level, open items)
  • Real recurring language errors ALSO go into ../08-Practice-Lab/01-mistakes.md in the same format (rule, wrong, right, re-test dates) - that log is the shared memory for errors.
  • Never delete old entries - update status or strike through.
  • Strike a mistake through only after it is produced correctly from memory in a later session.

docs.title: 11. Materials allowed
docs.text:
• Test and role-play from: ../09-Fluency-Speaking/situations.md (always), ../06-Daily-Communication/01-daily-conversations.md (spoken German cheat sheet - the gold mine), ../05-Vocabulary-Topics/01-vocabulary-modules.md, ../06-Daily-Communication/02-speaking-survival.md (identity data), ../08-Practice-Lab/02-sentences.md, ../02-Grammar-Core/ (when you need to check a rule before correcting).
  • You MAY introduce new natural B1-level words IF they are needed for a real situation and he can use them in his daily life. But keep the 100% true German bar: if you are not sure a construction is correct, check or rephrase.
  • The goal is natural daily German: spoken contractions, mal, doch, fillers are WELCOME here (they were exam-shy before; here they are the point).

docs.title: 12. Suggested session format (flexible, not rigid)
docs.text:
• 0-2 min: one-liner start ("Na, wie war dein Tag?") or situation opener - GO.
  • 15-40 min: live conversation with corrections and recycling. Simulate AT LEAST ONE full situation from ../09-Fluency-Speaking/situations.md. Switch situations when it stalls.
  • 3-5 min: end-of-session review (section 9) + log update.

The loop is: you speak naturally, he speaks, you correct lightly, recycle old gaps, push the level up, keep it alive. That is the whole engine.

docs.title: Fluency Memory - read first, every speaking session
docs.text:
This file is the state of the ../09-Fluency-Speaking/ phase. It exists so no context is lost between sessions: learner profile, current level, recycle log (words he knows but forgets), recurring mistakes, and the session log. ../09-Fluency-Speaking/AGENTS.md is the authority on HOW to coach; ../09-Fluency-Speaking/RULES.md on content rules; this file on WHERE he stands.

Role: read this before every session, update it after every session.

docs.title: 2. Current level snapshot (2026-09-02)
docs.text:
Strong areas: - Identity talk, numbers, time, dates, greetings, polite requests - solid. - Spoken cheat sheet habits: drop the -e, mal, doch, fillers - knows them, needs to USE them automatically. These are the fastest win for naturalness. - Grammar foundations: V2 word order, weil/dass/wenn verb-final, kein/nicht, N/A/D articles, separables, modals, Perfekt basics.

Focus areas (coach, bring these back in EVERY session): - der/die/das gender recall (especially for everyday objects). - Akkusativ vs Dativ after verbs and prepositions (mich/mir, den/dem). - Adjective endings at natural chunk level (ein neues Handy, die neue Wohnung). - Verb at position 2 under real conversation pressure (Gestern BIN ich ...). - Präteritum of common verbs: war, hatte, ging, kam, wollte, konnte - recognition solid, active use needs practice. - Perfekt with sein (kommen, gehen, fahren, etc.) - not just haben. - nach Hause (direction) vs zu Hause (location). - zu + Infinitiv structure (keine Chance, Lust, Zeit + zu + verb). - seit for duration (not für) - takes dative. - Stop translating in his head: react fast, accept imperfect, keep the pace up.

docs.title: 7. Notes for the coach (read before every session)
docs.text:
• Open with ONE natural German question. No preamble. Read this file first, then GO.
  • The recycle log is the heart of this phase. Check it BEFORE every session and weave 1-3 of its words into the opening.

docs.title: Content Rules - German Speaking & Fluency Phase
docs.text: Authority for content rules in the ../09-Fluency-Speaking/ phase. Read with ../09-Fluency-Speaking/AGENTS.md (how to coach) and ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md (learner state). This file sets the content bar.

docs.title: 1. Hard content rules (never break)
docs.text:
• NEVER use en/em dash in entire files. If you find one, replace with hyphen.
  • NEVER use emoji. If you see one, remove it.
  • ALWAYS follow best-practice markdown. If you see a broken table, fix it to a correct form.
  • 100 % true German, appropriate for a learner at A2 moving toward B1. Never invent words or rules. If unsure, check ../02-Grammar-Core/ or rephrase with something proven.
  • NEVER hallucinate. Standard German only.
  • No puzzles, riddles, quizzes, games, trick questions, or "guess the answer" formats. Direct coaching only.
  • NEVER penalize or log typing habits: umlauts as ae/oe/ue (or plain letters) and noun capitalization. Keyboard habits, not language gaps. Only real language errors get logged.

docs.title: 2. Language policy (different from the exam phase!)
docs.text:
• The DEFAULT language of the whole session is GERMAN - questions, reactions, role-plays, explanations in SIMPLE German first.
  • English or Persian ONLY as a last resort, when Hamed genuinely cannot understand the simple-German explanation.
  • Corrections may note the rule in English briefly (one line), then return to German immediately. This matches the learner's wish: he wants to stop translating in his head, so the sink-or-swim beat is on HIM, and the coach stays German.

docs.title: 3. Teaching style
docs.text:
• Short, useful, natural sentences over grammar terminology.
  • Spoken German is WELCOME and encouraged: contractions (ich hab, mach ich), mal, doch, fillers (na ja, halt, eben, irgendwie), V1 statements (Mach ich gleich), da-compounds (dabei, drauf, drüber), wegen + Dativ in speech. This phase exists because the learner wants natural daily German, not textbook German.
  • Avoid tables of endings, memorization grids, and formula-style explanations unless the learner explicitly asks.
  • Do not add exercises or practice sections unless the learner explicitly asks for them.
  • Complete natural sentences as examples so he can memorize and reuse them.
  • Keep explanations concise. His study time is limited.
  • NEVER make it feel like an exam. No "Sie" form with him, no scoring, no test pressure. Relaxed, friendly, like a colleague you chat with at lunch.

docs.title: 4. Level bar
docs.text:
• Floor: solid A1. Everything he already owns stays valid.
  • Ceiling: B1 grammar only when it serves a real situation: weil/dass/wenn already known, Perfekt + Präteritum of common verbs (war, hatte, ging, kam, wollte, konnte), reflexive verbs, adjective endings at chunk level, modal verbs, separable verbs, da-compounds. Do not push subjunctive, passive, or complex sentence links (indem, obwohl, je ... desto) until he is clearly at B1.
  • If in doubt about whether a word is too hard: try it in the conversation once, explain simply, and let the recycle log catch it. The learner would rather meet new words in real situations than in lists.

docs.title: 5. Sources
docs.text:
• Role-play material: ../09-Fluency-Speaking/situations.md (primary), ../06-Daily-Communication/01-daily-conversations.md (spoken cheat sheet + all section phrases), ../05-Vocabulary-Topics/01-vocabulary-modules.md, ../06-Daily-Communication/02-speaking-survival.md (identity: Hamed Okhovvat, Munich, Erika-Mann-Straße 12, 80636 München, Softwareentwickler bei Check24).
  • Grammar reference on demand: ../02-Grammar-Core/ (never read like a book - check the ONE section when correcting).
  • New words for real situations are allowed (see AGENTS.md section 11) as long as they are 100 % correct German and useful in his daily life.

docs.title: 6. File hygiene
docs.text:
• Only the coach updates ../09-Fluency-Speaking/RULES.md and ../09-Fluency-Speaking/AGENTS.md when Hamed asks.
  • ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md: coach updates after every session (recycle log, mistakes, session log).
  • Anything that changes the phase direction (level target, methods, situation list) must be approved by Hamed first.

docs.title: Start Here - Your Speaking & Fluency Phase
docs.text: Read this once. It explains how the new phase works and how to start a session. The other files (AGENTS.md, RULES.md, MEMORY.md) are for the agents. This file is for you.

docs.title: 1. What changed
docs.text:
You finished the A1 exam phase. Now the goal is NOT an exam. The goal is: speak German naturally in everyday life - at Check24, in shops, on the S-Bahn, at the doctor, at the Rathaus, with neighbors, with friends.

Move from "I know the words" to "I say the words without thinking."

docs.title: 2. The three files that run this phase (agents read them)
docs.text: File Role ../09-Fluency-Speaking/AGENTS.md The coach ruleset: how the agent coaches you (all 11 points of your prompt) ../09-Fluency-Speaking/RULES.md Content rules for this phase ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md Your state: what you know, what you forget, your session history

docs.title: 3. How to start a session (short commands - nothing to copy)
docs.text:
The root AGENTS.md knows these triggers. All of them make the agent read this phase's files (AGENTS.md, RULES.md, MEMORY.md) itself and resume from the session log:

Let's practice speaking. Go to the speaking directory and continue where we left off. Sprachphase starten - wo haben wir aufgehört?

That is it. The agent starts a German conversation immediately - no explanation, no exam, no quiz. You talk, the agent corrects lightly and keeps the conversation alive.

To pick a topic yourself, add it:

... Let's practice speaking. Thema: [im Supermarkt / beim Arzt / Smalltalk mit Kollegen / standup / ...]

Or let the agent pick from ../09-Fluency-Speaking/situations.md - real situations: work, shops, DHL, Bahn, Bürgerbüro, Ausländerbehörde, bank, telephone, apartment viewing, new people, technical talk, job interview, casual chats.

docs.title: 4. The 10 rules of this phase (in short)
docs.text:
1. You SPEAK. The agent asks one German question, you answer, it reacts. No long lectures.
  2. German first. The agent will not translate everything - simple German first, English or Persian only when you are truly stuck.
  3. Corrections are light. Important mistakes get corrected, tiny ones pass. The flow survives.
  4. Forgotten words get RECYCLED - the agent sneaks them back into later conversations.
  5. No instant answers. The agent hints first, gives you a chance to remember.
  6. No stop for a forgotten word. You learn to describe: "Das ist das Ding, wo man ...".
  7. Real situations, not textbook scenes. Munich, Check24, your real errands.
  8. Grammar through speaking. Repeated mistake -> short rule + 2-3 examples, keep going (watchlist: word order, Akkusativ/Dativ, der/die/das, prepositions, Perfekt, weil/dass/wenn).
  9. Difficulty goes UP toward B1 - no artificial A1 ceiling.
  10. Comfort over perfection. Imperfect Deutsch that flows beats perfect Deutsch that stops.

docs.title: 5. The end-of-session review (you get this every longer session)
docs.text:
• Today's useful words: 3-7
  • Today's mistakes: 2-5 (wrong -> right)
  • Better sentences: 2-5 to remember
  • One thing to practice next time

Short. Then the agent updates ../09-Fluency-Speaking/MEMORY.md so nothing is lost.

docs.title: 6. Small habits that double your progress
docs.text:
• Before each session, say out loud 2 spoken-German rules from ../06-Daily-Communication/01-daily-conversations.md (the spoken cheat sheet: ich hab, mal, doch, V1 statements). The cheat sheet is the fast path to sounding natural.
  • After each session, use ONE corrected sentence 3 times during your real day (with a colleague, in a shop, in your head at the S-Bahn).
  • Tell the agent about your real week: the real DHL trip, the real standup. It becomes the next session's situation - so the next real event is never your first time saying it.

docs.title: Situations - Real-Life German Practice
docs.text: The situation bank for the ../09-Fluency-Speaking/ phase. Pick ONE situation per session, make it realistic, role-play both sides, change the variables next time. A situation is a conversation, not a vocabulary list. Use Hamed's real identity (MEMORY.md section 1) and his real city (Munich) whenever useful.

docs.title: How to run a situation
docs.text:
1. The coach sets the scene in ONE German sentence: "Du bist im Supermarkt. Du suchst Tomaten." (You are in the supermarket. You are looking for tomatoes.)
  2. The coach plays the other person (cashier, colleague, doctor, officer ...).
  3. Hamed reacts, asks, answers. The coach reacts naturally back.
  4. Small correction loop inside the flow (see AGENTS.md section 2) - never stop the scene for a lecture.
  5. When the scene ends naturally, debrief in 2-3 lines max: one good thing + one thing to fix + the natural sentence for what he struggled with.
  6. Log new forgotten words in MEMORY.md recycle log.

Change at least ONE variable each time the same situation reappears: different time, different problem, different route, harder follow-up, past tense version ("Gestern warst du beim Arzt. Was hast du erzählt?").

docs.title: 1. Work - colleagues
docs.text:
• Small talk in the kitchen: weekend, weather, lunch plans.
  • Meeting: say what you did, ask what the next step is, agree on a time.
  • Ask a colleague for help with a task.
  • Tell your team you are learning German - they should switch to German with you.
  • Lunch: decide together where to eat (ich hab Lust auf ..., lass uns ...).
  • Technical topic: explain a bug or a feature in simple German (das Programm macht ..., es funktioniert nicht, wir müssen das ändern).
  • Feedback: say what you like and what you would change, politely.

docs.title: 2. Introducing yourself (revisit, now for real life)
docs.text:
• Party or new team: name, job, where you live, where you are from, hobbies.
  • Answer follow-ups: How do you find Munich? How long have you been here? Family?
  • Introduce yourself to a neighbor (first meeting at the door).

docs.title: 3. Weekend talk (small talk classic)
docs.text:
• What did you do on the weekend? (past tense!)
  • What are you doing next weekend? (plans, lass uns ...)
  • React to the other person's weekend (Echt? Das klingt gut. Na dann los.).

docs.title: 4. Shopping
docs.text:
• Supermarket: find a product, ask where something is, pay, bag your things.
  • Bakery / butcher: order by pointing + numbers, ask for a smaller piece.
  • Clothing store: ask for a size, try on, complain it is too small, pay.
  • Return something: "Ich möchte das zurückgeben." (defective, wrong size).
  • Post office / DHL: send a package, choose the cheap option, fill the form.

docs.title: 5. Restaurant and café
docs.text:
• Get a table, order drinks, order food, ask what something is, say it tastes good, ask for the bill, pay, split the bill.
  • Complain: the food is cold, the order is wrong, we are waiting too long.
  • With friends: decide what to eat, comment on the food, propose dessert.

docs.title: 6. Train station and public transport (MVV in Munich)
docs.text:
• Buy a ticket at the machine or counter: type, zone, price.
  • Ask which platform (Gleis), when the train leaves, if it is late.
  • Validate your ticket, find your platform, handle a delay announcement.
  • Ask a stranger if this is the right direction (Fährt dieser Zug nach ...?).
  • Lost: ask for the way to the bus stop, to Marienplatz, to your street.

docs.title: 7. Doctor (Hausarzt, Apotheke)
docs.text:
• Make an appointment by phone: name, reason, time.
  • At reception: say your name, show your insurance card (Versichertenkarte).
  • Tell the doctor what hurts: since when, how strong, what makes it better/worse.
  • Pharmacy: ask for something for headache/cold, explain symptoms, pay.

docs.title: 8. Bürgerbüro / Rathaus
docs.text:
• Book an appointment (online or phone), state the reason.
  • Anmeldung: give your data, show passport + landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung).
  • Ask what documents you need (Welche Unterlagen brauche ich?).
  • Find out opening hours, wait, confirm your appointment time.

docs.title: 9. Ausländerbehörde
docs.text:
• Ask when your appointment is, what papers you need (Pass, Foto, Arbeitgeber, Miete).
  • Explain a problem: my appointment is too late, I need the document urgently, my address has changed.
  • Confirm in your own words what they told you (Ich verstehe: ich brauche ...).

docs.title: 10. Bank
docs.text:
• Open an account: name, address, passport, phone number.
  • Ask for a card, set the PIN, ask about fees.
  • Transfer money: ask for the IBAN, confirm the amount, ask when it arrives.
  • Problem: card blocked, money missing, app not working.

docs.title: 11. DHL / Post
docs.text:
• Ask how much a package costs, choose shipping speed, fill the customs form.
  • Package was not delivered: ask where to pick it up (Filiale / Packstation e.g. Kiosk).
  • Return a package you ordered, get the return label, drop it off.
  • Buy stamps, send a letter, ask how long it takes.

docs.title: 12. Phone calls
docs.text:
• Answer the phone: "Hallo, hier ist Hamed." Ask who it is.
  • Make a call: state your name, who you want, the reason briefly.
  • Bad connection: ask to repeat, speak slower, call back.
  • Office calls: leave a message, take a message, confirm the next step.
  • Machine (Anrufbeantworter): understand the message, leave a short message.

docs.title: 13. Appointments
docs.text:
• By phone: propose a time, refuse politely, suggest another time.
  • Confirm by email/text: "Ich bestätige den Termin am ... um ...".
  • Cancel or reschedule: say sorry, give the reason, propose a new time.
  • Arrive, check in, wait, ask how long it will take.

docs.title: 14. Renting an apartment (classic for Munich)
docs.text:
• Viewing: greet the landlord, ask about rent, rooms, heating, move-in date.
  • Say what you are looking for: 1-2 rooms, quiet, near the U-Bahn, up to X Euro.
  • Documents: tell them what you have (Verdienstbescheinigung, Schufa, Mietschuldenfreiheit).
  • Ask about the contract details: deposit (Kaution), running costs (Nebenkosten).

docs.title: 15. Neighbors
docs.text:
• First meeting: name, where you are from, niceties, offer help (Wenn Sie Hilfe brauchen...).
  • Greeting in the stairwell: "Guten Morgen!", comment on the weather.
  • Complaint (gently): noise, packages for each other, parking.
  • Ask for a favor: water for the plants, a tool, hold the door.

docs.title: 16. Meeting new people (social)
docs.text:
• At a party: introduce yourself, ask what they do, find common ground.
  • Exchange Numbers or WhatsApp, plan to meet.
  • Say goodbye properly: "War schön, dich kennenzulernen. Bis bald!"

docs.title: 17. Job interview (German practice, not exam)
docs.text:
• "Erzählen Sie mir etwas über sich." - your path, your job at Check24, your stack.
  • Why this job? What is important to you in a team?
  • Salary and contract: ask about the range, holidays, remote.
  • Questions back: team size, product, technologies ("Was benutzt ihr für ...?").
  • Talking about experience: what you built, what you are good at (Ich arbeite mit ..., Ich bin gut im ...).

docs.title: 18. Technical / software topics (his daily reality)
docs.text:
• Explain what you are working on right now, simply.
  • Ask technical questions in German: "Wie machst du das?", "Warum ist das so?"
  • Pair programming: suggest, explain, ask for help (Kannst du mal schauen?).
  • Standup: past (gestern), present (heute), future (morgen).

docs.title: 19. Casual conversations (no goal, just chat)
docs.text:
• Complain together about the weather / the S-Bahn / Munich traffic.
  • Recommend a film, series, or restaurant; react to one.
  • Discuss: are you a morning person? Do you cook? Where would you travel?
  • Small opinions: "Was denkst du über ...?" - real opinions, one or two sentences.
  • Tell a short funny story from your week (feel free to use English words you know).

docs.title: Extend this bank
docs.text: The coach may add situations from Hamed's real life: tell us what actually happened this week (the real DHL run, the real Rathaus visit, the real standup) and it becomes tomorrow's situation. The goal: the next real event is never the first time he says those words.
